function: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) aggregation of satellite models: chooses which satellites upload (linkage scheme) and the HAP receive beamforming vectors under an MSE distortion limit (pp. 5-8).
system: 20 single-antenna LEO satellites (Starlink orbits) to 10 HAPs with L antennas (L=5, p. 16); no RIS; wavelength 15 mm, bandwidth 0.5 GHz (pp. 3, 9).
method: Bi-LSTM encoder plus MLP classifier trained with FedAvg made asynchronous (federated, supervised, IID); AirComp scheduling and beamforming by non-learned DFS/BFS search (pp. 6-10).
data_channel: Custom channel: Rician amplitude scaled by inverse squared HAP-satellite distance, uniform phase; Starlink TLE orbits; learning data MNIST and EuroSAT split IID (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and testing: 20 satellites, 1-10 HAPs, MSE threshold swept (15 dB in accuracy runs); no unseen scenario or dataset (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Own variants only: synchronous FL (FedAvg) and asynchronous FL, each with or without AirComp; exhaustive search as optimal reference; no earlier published scheme compared (pp. 10-13).
metrics: Training-data throughput, energy efficiency, global test accuracy and loss, time to reach 90% accuracy, convergence time, search complexity (pp. 10-13).
complexity: DFS linkage search O(2^M (M+2)) versus exhaustive O(4^M); BFS beamforming O((P/2)^L) versus O(P^L); M satellites, P phases, L antennas (pp. 7, 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "we assume the amplifications of channel coefficients are Rician distribution" (custom simulator with distance-based scale; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or measured channel is mentioned).
q2_support: p. 12: "In all scenarios, 20 satellites and 10 HAPs exist in the FL" (one fixed scenario and IID split; the number of HAPs and the MSE threshold are only swept, each setting a separate FL run; no unseen scenario or dataset).
q3_support: p. 9: "compare the proposed asynchronous FL framework and AirComp technique with synchronous FL framework" (only the paper's own variants, with or without AirComp; no earlier published over-the-air aggregation design is compared).
q4_support: p. 7: "the complexity of the DFS algorithm is" O(2^M (M+2)) versus O(4^M) for exhaustive search; the BFS beamforming search is O((P/2)^L) on p. 9.
q5_support: p. 10: "EuroSAT dataset is utilized as well" (MNIST and EuroSAT are datasets of the learning task alone, the channel is simulated, and no code or data link is given).
notes: Area 7 over 6 by precedence: the problem solved is the AirComp aggregation (linkage plus HAP receive beamforming) of an FL-trained classifier (pp. 3, 6). The learned element is the FedAvg-trained model; the DFS/BFS search is non-learned (pp. 7-9). HAPs have L antennas, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply (p. 16). The linkage scheduling is solved jointly with the physical-layer beamformer, so above_phy does not apply. Wavelength 15 mm is given but the band is not named (p. 9). Borderline q3: the synchronous FedAvg baseline is the paper's own variant of its framework, not an earlier published over-the-air design (pp. 9-10).
